messages.subject: Looping?
messages.body_plain:
G'day NichemapRs,

So in my endless quest teach myself both R and nichemapR, I've run into a problem that I really can't understand. Anybody who has seen this or solved it before, or would approach it differently and can advise me would be definitely deserving of a beer if I ever actually meet you anywhere. My problem is this:

I can now get the microclimate model to run at a single point by feeding it a latitude and longitude. From there I can run all the usual nichemapR things, the ectotherm model and the plantgrowth model and whatnot. What I want it to do now is to run those models for several locations (actually several hundred, but we'll start with several). I started with a simple for loop in R, thinking that it would just run through, extracting lat and long for each numbered location and generate the local microclimate and model the organism for that location (in this case a plant). It doesn't. Instead it runs through the micro_global model "i" times, generates "i" versions of the microclimate, one for each location, and then runs "i" plant models for the last location that it generated. So in the code below, even though it's given 5 locations, with 5 latlong codes (all lined up next to each other along an east-west gradient), it generates 5 versions of the plantgro models for the last point only.

I'm super confused about how and why it does this. I've written a lot of for loops in my life with a lot of different types of functions in them, and I've never seen a function that loops automatically within the loop. I've tried the edit(micro_global) command and can't see anything in there that looks like a loop to me. at least not one that should cause this. So my thoughts are that either there's a glitch in my for loop (I don't think so), for loops do something that micro_global can't handle, and I should be using an apply loop, which I find super confusing, or there's something else really weird going on that I've never seen before, so I don't recognise. Example script is below. Anybody who has 5 minutes (or hours, days, weeks or months) please help a brother out.

Cheers

Sean Tomlinson

pnt<-seq(1,5,1)
long<-as.numeric(list(113.4166,113.9166,114.2500,114.4166,114.5833))
lat<-as.numeric(list(-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335))

loop_plate<-cbind(pnt,long,lat)

l = as.numeric(max(loop_plate$pnt))
point=seq(1,l,by=1)

plant<-NULL

for (i in point){
    micro<-NULL
    micro<-micro_global(loc = c(as.numeric(loop_plate$long[i]),as.numeric(loop_plate$lat[i])), timeinterval = 365, nyears = 10, soiltype = 4,
                      REFL = 0.15, slope = 0, aspect = 0, DEP = c(0., 2.5,  5.,  10.,  15,  20,  30,  50,  100,  200), minshade = 0, maxshade = 90,
                      Usrhyt = 0.01)
    metout<-as.data.frame(micro$metout) # above ground microclimatic conditions, min shade
    shadmet<-as.data.frame(micro$shadmet) # above ground microclimatic conditions, max shade
    soil<-as.data.frame(micro$soil) # soil temperatures, minimum shade
    shadsoil<-as.data.frame(micro$shadsoil) # soil temperatures, maximum shade
    soilmoist<-as.data.frame(micro$soilmoist)
    soilpot<-as.data.frame(micro$soilpot)
    # append dates
    days<-rep(seq(1,12),24)
    days<-days[order(days)]
    dates<-days+metout$TIME/60/24-1 # dates for hourly output
    dates2<-seq(1,12,1) # dates for daily output

    minshade<-micro$minshad
    maxshade<-micro$maxshade

    generic_plant<-as.data.frame(plantgro(soilpot = soilpot, soilmoist = soilmoist, root_shallow = 4,
         root_deep = 8, growth_delay = 1, wilting_thresh = -200,
         permanent_wilting_point = -1500, FoodWater = 82))

    plant$point<-rbind(plant$point,i)
    plant$latitude<-rbind(loop_plate$lat[i])
    plant$longitude<-rbind(loop_plate$long[i])
    plant$moist<-rbind(plant$moist,mean(generic_plant$plantmoist))
    plant$plntwater<-rbind(plant$plntwater,mean(generic_plant$pct.water))
}

messages.body_plain:
Hello Sean,

I have had a look to your code. I have modified it to make it run for a n (n=5 in this case) number of locations. I do not know if I have coded to behave the way you wanted it to behave. If I have not just let me know if I can help you to fit your purpose. Here you have the code:

long<-as.numeric(list(113.4166,113.9166,114.2500,114.4166,114.5833))
lat<-as.numeric(list(-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335,-26.48335))

loop_plate<-cbind(long,lat)

# I am guessing that you want 5 different values for each location
plant <- data.frame(matrix(nrow=nrow(loop_plate), ncol=5))
colnames(plant) <- c('point','latitude','longitude','moist','plntwater')
head(plant)

for (i in 1:nrow(loop_plate)){
  micro<-micro_global(loc = loop_plate[i,], timeinterval = 365, nyears = 10, soiltype = 4,

                      REFL = 0.15, slope = 0, aspect = 0, DEP = c(0., 2.5,  5.,  10.,  15,  20,  30,  50,  100,  200), minshade = 0, maxshade = 90,
                      Usrhyt = 0.01)
  metout<-as.data.frame(micro$metout) # above ground microclimatic conditions, min shade
  shadmet<-as.data.frame(micro$shadmet) # above ground microclimatic conditions, max shade
  soil<-as.data.frame(micro$soil) # soil temperatures, minimum shade
  shadsoil<-as.data.frame(micro$shadsoil) # soil temperatures, maximum shade
  soilmoist<-as.data.frame(micro$soilmoist)
  soilpot<-as.data.frame(micro$soilpot)
  # append dates

  days<-rep(seq(1,12),24*365*10) # multiplied by timerinterval and nyears

  days<-days[order(days)]
  dates<-days+metout$TIME/60/24-1 # dates for hourly output
  dates2<-seq(1,12,1) # dates for daily output

  minshade<-micro$minshad
  maxshade<-micro$maxshade

  generic_plant<-as.data.frame(plantgro(soilpot = soilpot, soilmoist = soilmoist, root_shallow = 4,
                                        root_deep = 8, growth_delay = 1, wilting_thresh = -200,
                                        permanent_wilting_point = -1500, FoodWater = 82))

  plant[i,1] <- i
  plant[i,2] <- loop_plate[i,2]
  plant[i,3] <- loop_plate[i,1]
  plant[i,4] <- mean(generic_plant$plantmoist)
  plant[i,5] <- mean(generic_plant$pct.water)
}

plant

Hope it helps!

Cheers,
Urtzi

G'day Urtzi,

Damn that was quick mate. I turned away for a coffee and there you were with a fixed script. That does exactly what I was aiming at. I'm going to assume that the same plant data gets produced because the 5 locations are so close together. What I can't figure out is why your version works and mine doesn't. Yours is, I admit, much more elegant than my ham-fisted effort, but they seem pretty much semantically identical. I can't see which bit is tripping me over.

Another question associated with this data set: I have slope, aspect and soil types specifically associated with each location. I guess that if I bind these into the loop_plate matrix as columns 3,4 and 5 respectively then I can just code it up like this:

micro<-micro_global(loc = c(loop_plate[i,1],loop_plate[i,2]), timeinterval = 365, nyears = 10, soiltype = loop_plate[i,5],
                      REFL = 0.15, slope = loop_plate[i,3], aspect = loop_plate[i,4], DEP = c(0., 2.5,  5.,  10.,  15,  20,  30,  50,  100,  200), minshade = 0,

                      maxshade = 90, Usrhyt = 0.01)

I haven't pulled these data together yet, but now that the script seems to loop appropriately I'll give it a stab. Thanks very much for your help. Cheers

Sean

messages.body_plain:
Hello Sean,

Happy to help! Yes, I am sure that that coding might work for different aspect/slope/soil values too.

If I am not wrong, the only thing that was missing in your code was the arguments inside the brackets in the for() statement. I assume that if you change "for(i in point)" to "for(i in 1:point)" in your original code, it should also work. I just removed the code lines in which you created the "point" object because it was unnecessary. The "i" already gives you values from 1 to "n", being "n" your last point location.

All the best,
Urtzi
